Built for life in Porto

AI workflows iOS / Android Web app Personal project 2026

When I moved to Porto, I started using Claude Code to build small tools for the practical side of settling in: understanding what a mortgage really costs, learning Portuguese, and finding a home near a good school.

It was also a way to test AI-driven workflows in design and development, and to see how far each could go with Claude leading the build.

All three are personal tools, built for my own use rather than for clients.

Portuguese flashcards

Memeo is how I practise Portuguese every day. The content comes from the A1 course I took at university, and a few classmates ended up using it too, while others stuck with pen and paper.

Home, practice, verb conjugations and progress over time

The principle is simple: repetition builds memory. Cards are grouped by category, you answer by typing or speaking, every answer is checked, and you can hear the correct pronunciation. The app tracks the words you keep getting wrong and brings them back more often until they stick.

Memeo in action

I built it with Claude Code connected to Figma through MCP. Claude drafted the first screen, then turned it into a design system, tokens, styles and components that every other screen was built from. The finished app shipped to the App Store and Google Play.

Claude working through the component list in Figma, one component and screen at a time

The resulting design system: colour tokens for light and dark mode, and a type scale

Live on the App Store and Google Play

Mortgage calculator

Buying a house in Portugal means a broker's spreadsheet, ten banks moving at different speeds, and a layer of taxes and fees that is rarely explained in English. I built a dashboard with Claude Code to bring it all into one place.

The first step was structure. Emails, offers, appointment notes and broker messages became one consistent schema, and Portugal's lending rules, such as the Banco de Portugal debt-to-income stress test, became code, so every offer is assessed the same way.

Each bank's offer as one structured entry

The regulator's lending rule, written as code

Offers

The broker's comparison is re-priced against the house price and down payment I set. Each row is colour-coded, green for the best value and yellow-green for close behind, so the strongest offer stands out without reading every column.

Every offer re-priced for the same house, with the best value on each row in green

Estimation calculator

Using the offers and each bank's own lending rules, the calculator shows what is realistically within reach as you adjust house price, down payment and annual income.

Adjust income, price or down payment to see what it takes, and what it costs

Costs and timeline

A full breakdown of the mortgage and every fee on top of it, alongside a timeline of when each payment falls due.

Cash needed for the deal, the monthly payment, and when each amount is due

Buy vs rent

A sanity check on the whole decision: over a given time horizon, does buying actually beat renting?

Adjust rent, time horizon and growth assumptions to see which option comes out ahead

Status by bank

An overview of where each application stands, and the next step with every bank.

Ten banks in one table: the stage each application has reached and what comes next

Deal roadmap

Every step from choosing a house to getting the keys, with typical timings, so nothing in the process comes as a surprise.

The route from offer to keys, with typical timings for each step

Escolas do Porto

The third tool is an interactive map that scores neighbourhoods around Porto on the things that mattered to us. School performance in Portugal is publicly ranked, so the data was there to use.

Whenever a promising listing came up, we pasted in the address and could immediately see which schools served it and whether the area met our criteria.

Paste in an address to see the schools nearby and how each one ranks

Our criteria were distance to a good school, to the beach and to Porto, and access to public transport. Each has an adjustable tolerance, so we could tighten or relax them until the best areas stood out.

The order is deliberate: school first, then the beach. A zone with a strong school and a distant beach still ranks above an average school by the sea. Train access and the drive to Porto appear as supporting hints rather than changing the colour.

Rankings come from Público's national table of 9th-grade exam results. Because a school can move a hundred places in a single year, the map uses the weaker of the last two results. It also only counts the school a zone is actually assigned to, which reflects how enrolment works in Portugal. Every zone links directly to the homes for sale within it.

One zone in detail: its schools and rankings, the nearest beach and station, and the drive into Porto
